_readme: How the spreadsheet importer reads a worksheet (pipeline/external_sheet/layout.py).
The importer never hard-codes a tab name or a column letter. For EVERY
worksheet it finds the header row (the row in the first `headerScanRows`
whose cells match the most known header names below), maps each column to
a canonical field, and decides the tab's purpose from which fields are
present. Two-row headers are supported: a merged group label above
('Team 1') is prefixed to the sub-header below ('Ban 1' -> 'team 1 ban 1').
Header text is normalised before matching: lower-cased, accents removed,
punctuation turned into spaces, whitespace collapsed. 'Team 1 — Ban #2'
becomes 'team 1 ban 2'.
`fields` are single columns (exact match after normalisation).
`groups` are repeated column families matched by regular expression;
`{a}` / `{b}` / `{side}` expand to `sideTokens`. Named groups: side, p
(player position), n (list position), role.
When the real workbook changes shape, add the new header spelling here,
bump `version`, and run `python3 pipeline/sheet_sync.py rebuild` — the
committed raw cell layer is re-parsed without downloading anything.

map_rows.label: One row per map (teams, map, result, bans, hero columns)

player_rows.label: One row per player per map (listed heroes)

match_rows.label: One row per series (teams and series score, no map)

_forwardFill: Fields a block of rows may state once (a date over its maps). Team names are deliberately NOT forward-filled: a row with a blank team is reported, never attached to the previous row's team. Merged cells are expanded separately and always apply.
_tabPurposes: Tabs whose PURPOSE is decided by name, before anything else is tried (first match wins,
case-insensitive regex on the tab name). 'summary' = the sheet's own totals, which are
re-derived from the match cards and never imported; 'reference' = index tabs (hero / map
pictures, team rosters) and the Self-Check tab, read as lookups, never as matches.

_readme: The real community sheet is not a table: every series is a fixed-size MATCH CARD
(docs/SHEET-LAYOUT-NOTES.md). pipeline/external_sheet/cards.py finds each card by its
game label ('Week 1 | Day 2 | Game 3') and reads every value at a fixed offset from the
card's top row b (the row of the event label, `labelRow` rows above the game label).
Offsets are [row offset from b, column]. Left-panel columns are absolute letters; map
panel columns are offsets from the panel's first column (panel k starts at
`panels.firstColumn` + k * `panels.step`). Heroes are PICTURES, decoded through the
sheet's own Hero Index tab (picture, name in the cell below) plus the reviewed
`pictures` overrides in config/external/aliases.json. A picture nobody names stays an
unmapped hero; it is never guessed.
Not in the sheet, so never produced: calendar dates, who picked each map, any time.
matchCards._roleIcons: Role icons by picture hash. The Hero Index row-2 icons are read from the sheet itself (label to the right); the second colour set, used on the other team's rows, is listed here (probe run 5).
matchCards._banBlank: Ban cells that say no hero was banned (a forfeited map). Recorded as a flag on the map, never as a hero.

_readme: The sheet's own ground truth (tab 'Self-Check'): per stage and region, how many
matches and maps the editors count. After parsing, the importer compares its own
counts with these per row; a mismatch is a WARNING in the inventory, not a failure.
Columns are found by header text in the first `headerScanRows` rows; `columns` gives
the letters to fall back on when a header is not found.
selfCheck._columns: Probe run 6: row 2 headers 'Maps (Spreadsheet)' (H) and 'Matches (Spreadsheet)' (I); the stage is written once per group in B ('Stage 1' over its rows, so it is filled down) and the region code in D has no header (B2 says 'Region'). So stage and region are read by column letter.
